soluble and membrane‐bound IL‐15 Rα / IL‐15 complexes, but not soluble IL‐15, sustain the expansion of high‐avidicity CMV‐CTL for adoptive immunotherapies.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a cell‐based system for the generation of soluble and cell surface‐bound complexes of IL‐15 and its receptor, IL‐15Ralpha.
the generation of novel immunologically active cell lines for use as artificial antigen presenting cells (AAPC).
the development of novel strategies to enhance the efficacy of adoptively transferred T cells.

the use of soluble IL‐15 in combination with IL‐15 Rα in vitro and in vivo is not effective for the expansion of TCM cells.
the use of IL‐15 in combination with IL‐2 and IL‐7 for the expansion of T cells for adoptively transferred therapy of cancer and infections is warranted.
IL‐15R/IL‐15 is a very potent adjuvant to augment the efficacy of adoptively transferred T cells in cancer and infectious diseases.

IL‐15 is a potent adjuvent for enhancing the efficacy of adoptively transferred T cells.

the IL‐15/15Rα complex is superior to IL‐2 and IL‐7 as an adjuvant for the generation of T cells that are more potent, more specific and longer‐lived.
